detail.longDescription:
Attached: 1 image

I'm growing increasingly frustrated with the isolationist policy of Denmark.

It's bugging me on so many fronts, minor and (inter)national.

For the small: I can't buy batteries from China, I can't buy snus from Sweden (more choice, about 1/4 of the price) or any other country. I can buy Chinese batteries (most are), I just have to buy it from a Danish importer / drop shipping company, then it's OK for some reason. I bought a weather calendar from Australia, it was about $20, I ended up paying $60 in total for import taxes on a non-resellable, personal item.

For the larger: The university department I'm affiliated with has now  (top down, not a department decision) stopped teaching in English, in yet a further push to discourage international students. Not to mention that I've had discussions with quite a few international researchers who say it's an increasingly uphill battle to find positions on par with Danish nationals.

Don't get me wrong, there's a huge, nation-wide undercurrent of racism, and me as a male-presenting person of European descent hardly has to bear the brunt of it...but this is a relatively small country and having people want to come, live here, feel welcome seems kind of important.

Oh, and let's not forget this absolutely atrocious Orwellian campaign from the national security agency only 2 years back!

https://omnibus.au.dk/en/archive/show/artikel/pet-plakater-advarer-mod-spionage-paa-danske-universiteter-men-flere-forskere-kritiserer-kampagnen
